headline: AI agent hijacks, White House proxies and Binance heist dominate the Nov 5 briefing
overview: Today's shows lead with a Claude remote-control flaw, residential proxy traffic routed through White House networks, and a wave of breaches at Asian airlines via Amadeus. Supermarket and blood bank refrigeration tampering in Europe and France, and a French bank heist, add physical-impact concerns. Several shows also flag unpatched or actively exploited edge devices and a Linux TCP kernel flaw.

topStories.title: Claude remote-control flaw could enable device hijacking
topStories.summary: A researcher found that Anthropic's Claude Dispatch, which lets users control a desktop remotely, could be hijacked via an authenticated browser session to install a malicious package. The design weakness reportedly also touches related Claude features; Anthropic acknowledged it in May but has not fixed it.

topStories.title: Residential proxies running on White House networks
topStories.summary: Krebs on Security and Layer 3 Intel found proxy services renting White House IP addresses, with 236 connections recorded across 26 of 30 days. One provider has Russian links. The White House has not commented.

topStories.title: Amadeus breach exposes passenger data at six Asian airlines
topStories.summary: A cyber attack on the reservation provider Amadeus led to passenger data exposure at several airlines, including Japan Airlines, Korean Air and Singapore Airlines. Exposed fields can include passport and frequent flyer details; Amadeus reports no financial data access.

topStories.title: Refrigeration systems tampered with across Europe and in French blood bank
topStories.summary: Attackers remotely changed temperature settings on supermarket refrigeration in several European countries, and reportedly on equipment at French blood sites, where alarms caught the changes. No blood losses or patient harm were reported. Officials urge securing remote access and removing default passwords.

topStories.title: Edge device and patch alerts: Cisco, WatchGuard, Zyxel and SonicWall
topStories.summary: Cisco and WatchGuard shipped patches for critical flaws, with Cisco noting an actively exploited issue across 19 products. Zyxel GS1900 switches were hit by a zero-day used against nearly a thousand devices, and SonicWall's end-of-life GMS platform has unpatched flaws.

topStories.title: Linux kernel TCP flaw and APT signature bypass
topStories.summary: A remote root-level flaw in the Linux TCP stack affects many distributions, with some vendors still preparing fixes. Separately, an APT signature bypass lets attackers push swapped packages to Debian and Ubuntu systems via forced retries.

episodes.title: Claude, you've got company.
episodes.summary: Covers the Claude dispatch hijack, White House residential proxies, the Amadeus-linked airline breaches, Cisco and WatchGuard patches, the GhostMap Android reboot flaw, a Zyxel zero-day, Ukrainian call centre arrests, AI-driven pet scams and a guilty plea in an Ethiopia espionage case. Also includes a sponsored interview with the CEO of QSecure on NIST's post-quantum migration timeline.

episodes.title: Ballots, bots, and backlash.
episodes.summary: Covers election-day security attempts, European refrigeration attacks, OpenAI security criticism, NVIDIA's China customer limits, the Binance heist, a Barracuda flaw, Gartner's SOC staffing forecast and an indictment of two Canadian hackers. Includes a sponsored Box CISO interview on enterprise AI governance.

episodes.title: Blood bank fridge hacks, Anthropic model identity, Google Calendar phishing
episodes.summary: Covers French blood bank fridge tampering, Anthropic's model-verification research prototype, Google Calendar phishing that bypasses MFA, a China-aligned keyboard app hijack, a French bank heist, APT29-linked mobile exploits, a tampered game launcher and a hacked Ukrainian news site. One segment is sponsored by ESET.

episodes.title: SANS Stormcast Thursday, November 5th, 2026: Email Test Scripts; runZero oobscan BMC/IPMI; apt Signature Bypass (CVE-2026-109518); SonicWall GMS EOL Unpatched Flaws
episodes.summary: Covers exposed test email scripts leaking configuration and enabling spam, the OOBScan tool for finding exposed out-of-band management interfaces, an APT signature bypass, and unpatched SonicWall GMS flaws.

episodes.title: Why a Data Center Slowdown Benefits Big Tech
episodes.summary: Discusses the midterm results and data centre politics, and whether a slowdown could benefit large cloud providers. Also covers ChatGPT search growth, acquisitions and bank agent payments. Segments are sponsored; the rest is commentary on AI and markets.

episodes.title: How the Midterm Results Change AI
episodes.summary: Analyses how the midterm results may shape AI policy, focusing on data centre opposition, key Senate and state races, and likely incremental regulation. This is opinion and analysis rather than reported events.

episodes.title: That's Not Supposed to Happen - PSW #951
episodes.summary: A roundup of supermarket refrigeration attacks, a Linux TCP flaw, the Binance theft, PHP security debt, a Google Android TV botnet takedown, and AI-assisted exploit development, among other items. The notes list topics only, without detail.

episodes.title: Zyxel 2nd Switch 0-Day, 1K Hacked, Debian/Ubuntu APT MitM Flaw, France Blood Supply Cyberattack
episodes.summary: Lists a second Zyxel switch zero-day, a Debian and Ubuntu APT man-in-the-middle flaw and the French blood supply attack, alongside AI-linked breaches and Chrome 157 fixes. Notes are headline-only with little detail.

episodes.title: APT29-linked phone exploits, Zyxel patch bypass, White House proxy | Cyber Security News Nov 5
episodes.summary: Covers APT29-linked exploitation of unpatched phones, the Zyxel GS1900 flaw being used since August, a DreamHost file manager credential exposure, the APT retry flaw, Xen hypervisor memory flaws and a White House proxy issue. Recommends patching and device minimum-version controls.

episodes.title: Hospital Diverts Ambulances, 5.7M Breached by a Phone Call, Town Pays $82K Ransom
episodes.summary: Covers a ransomware attack that diverted ambulances from a New Mexico trauma centre, and a phone-based social engineering breach affecting about 5.7 million people. The notes end partway through, so later stories are not covered.

episodes.title: How AI agents are spooking the banks
episodes.summary: Covers AI agents calling banks on users' behalf, a ransomware recovery fraud case, and a sponsored interview on AI-driven alert triage. The notes are a transcript of the show's content.

episodes.title: ARTEX for Everyone: What Widely Available AI Hacking Means for Defenders
episodes.summary: Discusses the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework, which is openly available and now appearing in real intrusions, and defensive steps such as credential rotation and exposure management. This is a sponsored discussion from a vendor.

episodes.title: Stolen Entra app secrets, cPGuard update hijack, Binance fake interview | Cyber Security News Nov 4
episodes.summary: Covers stolen Entra app secrets used for sign-ins through MSPs, a hijacked CPGuard update channel, a Node-RED exploitation campaign, WS_FTP admin credential exposure and Chrome 157 fixes. Recommends rotating secrets and checking sign-in logs.

episodes.title: 🎙️ Linux Kernel TCP Use-After-Free Gives Remote Unauthenticated Root on Every Major Distribution, Barracuda Critical Flaws Allow Root Access to Security Appliances, Google Dismantles 1.3 Million Devi
episodes.summary: Covers a remote root Linux TCP flaw, Barracuda root flaws, a 1.3 million device Android botnet takedown, Android's November updates and a password manager incident. Notes are headline-only.
